guideline: Four criteria: (1) Preference, (2) Coherence, (3) Consistency, (4) Fluency.
Human annotators evaluate translations according to four criteria: Preference, Coherence, Consistency, Fluency.

We use four criteria for human evaluation: (1) Preference measures whether the translation preserves the role preference information; (2) Coherence denotes whether the translation is semantically coherent with the dialogue history; (3) Consistency measures whether the lexical choice of translation is consistent with the preceding utterances; (4) Fluency measures whether the translation is logically reasonable and grammatically correct.
